method_note: I rebuilt the r3 verdict's probe from its own description (lum>0.06 on the linear-ish Rec.709 luma, 8-connectivity, components dropped if bbox width >0.35*frame or area >1500 px) and it reproduces the predecessor's r3 numbers EXACTLY (15-fast n=152 / 1623 px / med 4.0 / 51.3% <=4px / 21.1% >=16px / 76.3% sat>=0.45; 16-slow n=128 / 1096 px / med 3.0 / 63.3% / 15.6% / 77.6%). So every r3->r4 delta below is like-for-like. That probe is now DEGENERATE on the slow frame, however: its single excluded mega-component (the bloom halo + blade streak + fruit, connected) grew 27809 -> 48184 px in r4 because the slow cleave's ligaments are all attached to it, leaving only n=28 / 70 px of 'free droplets' in 16-slow. That is precisely the 'the failure hides in the excluded class' hazard, so I added an ALL-PARTICLE probe: high-pass (lum minus gaussian sigma=5) > 0.030 to separate high-frequency particles from the smooth bloom, minus the fruit body (largest CC of open(lum>0.15, disk 11), dilated 6). Both probes run over r3 and r4 identically.

predecessor_probe_free_droplets.note: Colour axis on this probe: 76.3% vs 77.6% (r3 dead heat) -> 13.8% vs 94.3% (r4). That is an 80.5-point separation in the correct direction. Size axis on this probe is unreadable in r4 because 16-slow retains only 70 free-droplet pixels.

all_particle_probe_offbody.confound_noted: 15-fast is a citrus and 16-slow is a watermelon, so juice hue differs by construction. The size axis is unaffected by that; the colour axis is not purely a stroke-speed measurement. It survives anyway because 09-combo+50ms (mixed fruit, fast swipe) measures 82.4% <=4px / 2.9% >=16px / 23.7% sat>=0.45 / meanSat 0.257, i.e. the fast morphology is not tuned to the citrus asset.

central_test_15_vs_16.threshold_robustness: Across thr 0.06/0.10/0.15/0.20/0.30 on the free-droplet probe, 15-fast's sat>=0.45 runs 13.8/2.5/0.2/21.0/8.2% and 16-slow's runs 94.3/87.3/84.5/73.6/40.6%. The colour separation holds at every threshold; it is not an artefact.

sheet_envelope.conclusion: Genuinely improved, not fixed. The r3 shape was monotonic to a peak at +500 ms; r4 peaks in the +100..250 ms window and is at 2.0% of peak by +500 ms and literally zero by +1000 ms. The remaining defect is the leading edge: at +33 ms the frame carries 671 px, 14% of its own peak, so the film is still ramping IN when the bar (R2) wants it at full extent by 30-40 ms. Median blob area at +100 ms is 21.5 px with 60% of blobs >=16 px and 76.3% juice-tinted, which is the fat-red-lozenge population, not a film.

evidence.blind_test: Instant on five of the seven fluid frames, and the two that hesitate are the two that got the fix. 00-hero.png is decided in well under a second: roughly 200 red lozenges, all the same smooth ellipse, all carrying one bright bead of specular, evenly scattered over a black field with white pill-shaped dots interleaved — you can count them, and plate-01's droplets cannot be counted because they range from sub-pixel mist to a fifth of the watermelon and half of them are mid-pinch-off ligaments rather than spheres. 04-cut+250ms is the same field with the density turned down; 03-cut+100ms adds a flat red translucent fan that reads as a decal. 16-slow-cleave+50ms is a starburst of red spikes radiating from a melon and reads as a Fruit Ninja splat effect. Against that, 15-fast-flick+50ms is the best frame this project has produced: a fine achromatic wedge hugging the cut plane off an orange, correctly white, correctly heavy-tailed to tiny, correctly directional. It still loses, in about two seconds, on DENSITY and on the blade: plate-02's aerosol is a continuum in which no individual grain is resolvable, ours is ~200 resolvable specks with black gaps between them, and our blade is a full-width glowing horizontal ribbon where R1b's is a solid object with a thin edge highlight. 09-combo+50ms is the second-best frame for the same reason.

evidence.what_did_not_move: The bead/droplet impostor itself. fluid.js:451-463 correctly ORBITS the specular so it is not a static sprite, and 475 mixes white->juice by size as the bar demands — but the silhouette is still one smooth analytic ellipse for every particle at every size. fix: One file, /home/claude/juice/src/juice/fluid.js, and it is the droplet IMPOSTOR, not the emitter counts — the counts and the tint law are now measurably right and further tuning of them will not buy a point.
